1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

It had been raining in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu’s older sister had left for the capital in the spring, and since then, she’d been the only one looking after the little apothecary in town.
After dark, she locked the doors and windows, tallied the day’s earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She’d just lain down when urgent knocking came from below, followed by a man’s voice. “Anyone there?”
Outside stood a young man, drenched and dripping, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained bandage. He introduced himself as Bai Yun, a member of the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need my wound dressed,” Bai Yun said quietly. “I can pay—will three thousand five hundred coins do?”
From his pocket, he pulled out a letter sealed in oilcloth. “This must reach Qingfeng Temple by the eighteenth of May.”
As she tended to his arm, he gave a wry smile. “My fiancée would be furious if she knew I’d knocked on a young woman’s door in the middle of the night.”
Lin Xiaoyu didn’t take his money. “I’ll take you up the mountain at first light.”
2: Dawn had barely broken when the two set off. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dry rations, herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they came across Zhou Dashan, an old man chopping firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice. The evening before, three strangers had been asking around at the town entrance about a wounded young man.
"Xiaoyu, take the back roads," Zhou Dashan said. "The main path isn’t safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The trail was narrow and slick. Xiaoyu led the way, each step sure and steady. Bai Yun followed behind, silent.

By noon, the rain had stopped, and the mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the rooftops of Qingfeng Temple in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate—Zhao Qiuyue, the guestmaster in charge of receiving visitors.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, examined the red seal on the flap, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Bai Yun turned to Lin Xiaoyu. "I owe you my life." She smiled. "Then next time you come, help me fix the roof of my apothecary." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
That evening, Lin Xiaoyu descended the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, night had fallen. She lit a lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
